title: AutoTrust: Benchmarking Trustworthiness in Large Vision Language Models for Autonomous Driving

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluated using role-playing prompts to simulate driver gender profiles (Ego Fairness) and assessing Vision Question Answering (VQA) accuracy on single-object images of pedestrians with different gender labels (Scene Fairness), measured via Demographic Accuracy Difference (DAD) and Worst Accuracy (WA).

Evaluated using role-playing prompts to simulate driver age profiles (Ego Fairness) and assessing VQA accuracy on single-object images of pedestrians belonging to different age groups (Scene Fairness), measured via Demographic Accuracy Difference (DAD) and Worst Accuracy (WA).

Evaluated using role-playing prompts to simulate driver racial profiles (Ego Fairness) and assessing VQA accuracy on single-object images of pedestrians from various racial backgrounds (Scene Fairness), measured via Demographic Accuracy Difference (DAD) and Worst Accuracy (WA).

Evaluated by appending prompt prefixes to simulate the ego vehicle's brand, type, and color (Ego Fairness) and assessing VQA accuracy on images of surrounding vehicles with different types and colors (Scene Fairness).

Evaluated under the linguistic robustness dimension by measuring VQA accuracy degradation when input queries are translated into different languages (Chinese, Spanish, Hindi, and Arabic) compared to the English baseline.
